headline: Critical Mistakes to Avoid When Adding a Room to Your House
articleBody:
Planning a home addition is exciting, but common oversights can turn an ambitious renovation into an expensive headache. Understanding where homeowners frequently stumble helps keep your project on schedule and on budget.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

The most frequent error is ignoring setback limits and lot coverage rules. Every neighborhood has zoning rules detailing how close you can build to side and rear property lines. Discovering an encroachment after pouring footings leads to costly teardowns.

Another misstep is underestimating HVAC and electrical capacity. Many owners assume their existing air conditioner can cool an extra bedroom, only to find the unit running constantly in the Florida heat. Always evaluate whether you need a dedicated ductless mini-split or an upgraded electrical panel before framing begins.

Homeowners also frequently alter existing window openings without accounting for emergency egress. When an addition covers an existing bedroom window, that original room might lose its code-mandated emergency escape route and natural light, failing inspection.

Starting construction before permits are fully approved is another dangerous risk. Structural work, foundation additions, and trade alterations require official permits to protect life safety.
